message.content: Fusion research has already produced practical benefits by advancing high temperature superconductors, vacuum engineering, and materials that resist intense neutron damage. The same plasma diagnostics developed for tokamaks now help monitor industrial processes, improve medical imaging, and support secure nuclear waste analysis. High power radio frequency systems created for ion heating have become useful in semiconductor manufacturing and in advanced additive manufacturing. Large scale cryogenic and low carbon refrigeration projects for fusion prototypes have also informed green industrial cooling and hydrogen production. These iritic insights also strengthen engineering capacity and clean energy readiness.
